seo.title: The Linux Command That Explains A 'Slow' Server In 5 Seconds
seo.hook: CPU idle, machine stuck. Here is why.
seo.description: vmstat's si/so columns show memory being pushed to disk. Sustained swap-out means you need RAM, not CPU.

scenes.narration: The C P U looks idle. The machine feels stuck. One command tells you why in about five seconds.

|V M stat one prints one sample a second. ^The very first row is an average since the machine booted, so ignore it completely — it is history, not a reading of now. ~The columns that matter are S I and S O: swap in, and swap out. Zero there means memory is keeping up. ^Anything sustained above zero means the kernel is pushing memory to disk to stay alive, and disk is thousands of times slower than RAM. That climb is why the machine feels stuck while the C P U looks idle.
